notes: The exchange is stateless request/response: handle_request derives its answer entirely from the request string and the Cache passed in, with no session or handshake, so `states` is empty (kvstore/src/api.rs:15-33).

No timeouts are observable. The `ttl_secs` field of `put` is parsed as a u64 and then stored only as the literal string `ttl=<n>`; nothing reads it back or expires an entry, so it does not drive a state transition (kvstore/src/api.rs:27-28).

kvstore/src/cache.rs and kvstore/src/storage.rs are modeled as internals of the `store` participant, not as separate parties: the Cache is called in-process by handle_request, and FileStore is not reachable from the CLI path at this revision (kvstore-cli/src/main.rs:3-11).

FileStore defines an on-disk layout (one file per key under `root`) and a little-endian u32 magic-number reader, but no producer of that format exists in this repository and the CLI never constructs a FileStore, so it is recorded as context rather than as a protocol participant (kvstore/src/storage.rs:20-49).

protocol.framing: one request per argv element; colon-separated fields (`verb:arg[:arg]`)

messages.name: put:<key>:<ttl_secs>
messages.schema: put:<key>:<ttl_secs>  — ttl_secs is parsed as u64 and stored as the literal value `ttl=<ttl_secs>`

messages.name: Response::Ok(String)
messages.schema: Ok(<value>) — the cached value for a `get`

participants.description: The kvstore-cli binary. Builds a Cache, takes each command-line argument after argv[0] as one wire request, hands it to handle_request, and prints the debug rendering of the Response to stdout.
participants.name: client

participants.description: The kvstore library's request-handling layer. Splits the request on ':', dispatches on the verb, and answers from the in-memory Cache. Wire requests are documented as untrusted input.
participants.name: store
